registers.label: Spare
lines: One sheep wandered off, and the shepherd left the ninety-nine to find it.
He lays it on his shoulders and carries it home rejoicing.
A woman lit a lamp and swept the house until the lost coin gleamed.
Rejoice with me; what was lost is found.
Christ Jesus came to save sinners, and we are not too far gone for grace.
Mercy reached the worst of us; mercy reaches us still.
Come, you who were found, and worship.
There is joy in heaven over us. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture a woman on her knees with a lamp, sweeping every corner of a dark house, fingers brushing the floor for one small coin.
Rejoice with me; what was lost is found.
And when it catches the light at last, she does not pocket it quietly — she runs to the neighbors, calling everyone to be glad.
Rejoice with me; what was lost is found.
So it is with the shepherd and the strayed sheep, hoisted onto his shoulders and carried home; so it is in heaven over one who turns back.
Rejoice with me; what was lost is found.
However far off you have felt this week, hear this: Christ came for sinners, and mercy has come looking for you. You are found.
Rejoice with me; what was lost is found. Thanks be to God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The shepherd carries the lost one home on his shoulders.
What was lost is found.
A lamp is lit; the swept house gives up its coin.
What was lost is found.
Christ came for sinners; mercy came for us.
What was lost is found.
Come, you who were found, and worship.
What was lost is found. Amen.
